title_en: The ruling on praying after ʿAsr
body_ar:
ما قولكم في شأن الصلاة بعد العصر وقبل المغرب؟

أن البخاري ومسلما أخرجا في الصحيحين من حديث ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال شهد عندي رجال مرضيون وأرضاهم عندي عمر بن الخطاب أن رسول الله (ص) نهى عن الصلاة بعد الفجر حتى تطلع الشمس وبعد العصر حتى تغرب، وقد بين النبي (ص) في حديث عمرو بن عبسة رضي الله عنه أوقات النهي عن الصلاة، فأمره أن يصلي إذا طلع الفجر، وأن يكف بعد ذلك حتى إذا ارتفعت الشمس قيد رمح وزالت عنها الحمرة فليصل، حتى إذا قام قائم الظهيرة فليكف، حتى إذا صلى العصر فليكف، حتى إذا غربت الشمس فليصل..

وحذر النبي (ص) من الصلاة ودفن الموتى وقت طلوع الشمس ووقت غروبها وعندما يقوم قائم الظهيرة، كما في حديث ابن عمر في الصحيحين ثلاث ساعات نهينا أن نصلي فيها وأن نقبر فيها موتانا، واختلف العلماء في درجة النهي، فذهب جمهورهم إلى أن الأوقات التي النهي فيها شديد على سبيل الحرمة تبطل الصلاة فيها نفلا كانت، ورأى أبو حنيفة بطلانها مطلقا سواء كانت فرضا أو نفلا، فمن طلعت عليه الشمس وهو في صلاة الصبح مثلا كمن لم يستيقظ إلا ذلك الوقت فصلاته باطلة عند أبي حنيفة صحيحة عند الجمهور، وكذلك من غربت عليه الشمس وهو في صلاة العصر فإن صلاته باطلة عند أبي حنيفة ويستأنفها بعد أن تختفي الشمس، وعند الجمهور صلاته صحيحة لقول النبي (ص): من نسي صلاة أو نام عنها فليصلها متى ما ذكرها فإن وقتها ذكرها، فإن الله تعالى يقول: {وأقم الصلاة لذكري}.
body_en:
What do you say concerning prayer after ʿAsr and before Maghrib?

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "Men whose testimony I accept bore witness to me — and the most acceptable of them to me was ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab — that the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, forbade prayer after Fajr until the sun rises, and after ʿAsr until it sets." The Prophet, upon whom be peace, set out the times in which prayer is forbidden in the hadith of ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah, may God be pleased with him: he commanded him to pray when dawn breaks, and then to refrain, until, when the sun has risen the length of a spear and its redness has left it, let him pray; then, when the sun stands at its zenith, let him refrain; then, when he has prayed ʿAsr, let him refrain; then, when the sun has set, let him pray..

The Prophet, upon whom be peace, warned against praying and against burying the dead at the time the sun rises, at the time it sets, and when the sun stands at its zenith — as in the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar in the two Ṣaḥīḥs: "Three hours in which we were forbidden to pray and to bury our dead." The scholars differed as to the degree of this prohibition. The majority of them held that the times in which the prohibition is severe are so by way of forbiddenness (ḥurmah), and that prayer performed in them is void (bāṭil), it being a voluntary prayer. Abu Hanifah held it to be void without qualification, whether it was an obligatory or a voluntary prayer. So one upon whom the sun rises while he is in the dawn prayer — as with one who did not wake until that time — his prayer is void according to Abu Hanifah, and valid according to the majority. Likewise one upon whom the sun sets while he is in the ʿAsr prayer: his prayer is void according to Abu Hanifah, and he begins it afresh after the sun has disappeared; while according to the majority his prayer is valid, because of the saying of the Prophet, upon whom be peace: "Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it whenever he remembers it, for its time is when he remembers it" — for God Most High says: {And establish the prayer for My remembrance} (Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:14).

flags.context: فذهب جمهورهم إلى أن الأوقات التي النهي فيها شديد على سبيل الحرمة تبطل الصلاة فيها نفلا كانت، ورأى أبو حنيفة بطلانها مطلقا سواء كانت فرضا أو نفلا
options: prayer performed in them is void, it being a voluntary prayer
prayer performed in them is void if it is a voluntary prayer
prayer performed in them is void, be it voluntary [or obligatory]
flags.note: CRITICAL — the scope of the majority's ruling turns on this clause. The Arabic 'naflan kānat' is elliptical and the contrast drawn immediately afterwards with Abu Hanifah ('muṭlaqan, whether obligatory or voluntary') indicates that the majority's voiding is confined to voluntary prayer, which favours option 1. But the clause reads as though a word has dropped out of the source, and option 2 would reverse the scope and so misattribute a much stronger ruling to the majority. Option 0 is the most literal and least committal. Needs checking against the Sheikh's original.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.

The date shown by the CMS (27 December 2010) is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

The Sheikh reports the disagreement between the majority and Abu Hanifah and does not state his own preference in this text. The English does not resolve it. The hadith cited last is the majority's supporting evidence, not a statement of his own position, and must not be displayed as though it were.
'Three hours' renders 'thalāth sāʿāt' — 'hours' here means periods of time, not clock hours.
'The sun stands at its zenith' renders 'qāma qāʾim al-ẓahīrah', literally the moment at which the midday shadow ceases to shorten.
